To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) electrospinning is a versatile and effective method to produce nanofibers with controllable diameters, morphologies, and properties for toughening and damage healing applications in polymer matrix composites, (2) nanofibers can be produced by electrospun ning and solution blowing with a wide range of fiber diameters and morphologies, and these nanofibers are effective in enhancing the interlaminar toughness of polymer matrix composites with different matrix materials, fiber orientations

(a) electrospun and solu tion blown nanofibrous interlayers are effective in enhancing the interlaminar mechanical properties of laminated PMCs, (b) the interfacial damage healing of PMCs can be achieved through the incorporation of healing agents into nanofibrous layers, (c) the healing agent loaded nanofi brous layers can also enhance the interlaminlar mechanical properties of the laminated PMCs through the toughening effect of the healing agents,

1) nanofiber reinforced resin rich interlayers can significantly increase interfacial toughnesses and 2) nanofiber rich interlayers with core shell healing agents can heal interfacial cracks and delamina tions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the toughening and damage healing of polymer matrix composite (PMC) laminates with electrospun and/or solution blown nanofiber riched interlayers.
the development and characterization of advanced interlayers for interfacial damage toughening and self healing of laminated PMCs.
the fabrication of advanced nanoscale reinforcements and their use to enhance the mechanical and damage self healing properties of high performance polymer matrix com posite laminates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the interfacial tough ening and damage self healing in PMCs reinforced with continuous nanofibers can be achieved through the following two approaches: (1) the interlaminar toughening approach and (2) the interfacial self healing approach.

the interfacial toughen ing and damage self healing properties of polymer nanofiber reinforced PMCs have been greatly advanced by the recent developments in the scalable, continuous production of polymer and carbon nanofibres.
there has been a great deal of progress in the toughening and damage healing of polymer com posites with electrospun and/or solution blown nanofiber reinforced interfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using nanofiber reinforced composites to improve the interlaminar properties of laminated composites.
our group has made significant contributions to the understanding of the role of interphase in the mechanical behavior of composites.
we have developed a scalable, continuous, and low-cost process for the fabrication of advanced nanomaterials for toughening and self healing of PMC interfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incorporation of nanofibers into the resin rich interlayers of high performance polymer composites (PMCs) can significantly increase their interlaminar toughnesses.
the incorporation of nanofiber rich interlayers into high performance laminated composites can yield a unique damage self healing effect at interlaminar interfacial regions.

the incorporation of nanofiber rich interlayers can significantly enhance the interlaminar toughness and damage healing capability of high performance PMCs, and the scalable, continuous production of advanced nanofiber reinforced composites is feasible.
